findings.claim: A mutual-hedging loop is visible: each low-commitment signal ("no pressure", "if it works out", "it's whatever") is met with an equally low-commitment reply, so neither side ever has to be the one who visibly wanted more.
evidence_refs: we should grab coffee sometime, no pressure
sure, if it works out. I'm pretty busy this week
same, it's whatever, just figured I'd mention it

findings.claim: The loop can produce a false shared reality where both people privately assume the other is not interested, even if one or both would actually welcome plans, because neither move ever gets tested.
evidence_refs: let me know if you're around

findings.claim: A possible exit from the loop is for either party to name a concrete day and time instead of leaving the next move open-ended.
evidence_refs: let me know if you're around

findings.claim: probe: one of them proposing a specific day and time in a follow-up message would discriminate between genuine low interest, which would likely be met with another vague deflection, and performed indifference, which would likely be met with quick acceptance.
evidence_refs: sure, if it works out. I'm pretty busy this week
let me know if you're around
